</analysis>

<summary>

1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user requested completion of a three-phase FreeLang language development project. Phase 1 (195 built-in functions) was pre-completed. User explicitly requested Phase 2 (JavaScript Interpreter) completion with "시작" (start), then explicitly requested Phase 3 (Standard Module System) with "go 3", and finally issued "go" to continue Phase 3 work. The ultimate goal is to create a complete, production-ready FreeLang language implementation with 385+ functions across core interpreter and standard library modules.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Three-layer interpreter architecture: Lexer (tokenization) → Parser (AST generation) → Evaluator (execution)
   - Module loader pattern with require() system similar to Node.js
   - Environment-based lexical scoping with closure support
   - Control flow signals (ReturnValue, BreakException, ContinueException) for implementing return/break/continue
   - Operator precedence handling in recursive descent parser
   - Cryptographic operations using Node.js crypto module
   - Synchronous and asynchronous file I/O operations
   - Path manipulation for cross-platform compatibility
   - Hash functions (MD5, SHA-256, HMAC) and symmetric encryption (AES, DES)

3. Files and Code Sections:

   **Phase 2 Files (JavaScript Interpreter)**:
   - src/lexer.js (1,104 lines)
     - 60 token types defined in TokenType object
     - Character classification functions (isDigit, isAlpha, etc.)
     - Complete tokenization with line/column tracking
     - Comment handling (line and block comments)
     - Key method: tokenize() returns array of Token objects
   
   - src/parser.js (1,237 lines)
     - Recursive descent parser with 20+ parser methods
     - AST node classes for all language constructs
     - Operator precedence: assignment → conditional → logicalOr → ... → primary
     - Critical fix: Removed postfix operator parsing from postfix() method (was incorrectly treating + and - as postfix operators)
     - Critical fix: Added consumeSemicolon parameter to variableDeclaration() for handling for loop init
     - Critical fix: Changed for loop parsing to check for for-in first (no parentheses) before regular for (with parentheses)
     - Critical fix: Wrapped function body statements in BlockStatement for proper execution
   
   - src/evaluator.js (582 lines, modified)
     - Environment class for scope management
     - FreeLangFunction class for user-defined functions with closure support
     - Critical fix: Changed CallExpression evaluation to check `instanceof FreeLangFunction` before `typeof === 'function'`
     - Added moduleLoader import and require() function injection into globalEnv
     - Full support for: binary/unary/logical operations, function calls, member access, control flow (if/while/for/for-in)
   
   - src/interpreter.js (86 lines)
     - Main entry point: FreeLangInterpreter class
     - Integrates Lexer → Parser → Evaluator pipeline
     - execute() method returns {success, result, error}
     - repl() method for interactive mode
     - executeFile() method for running .fl files
   
   - test_phase2_interpreter.js (677 lines) and test_phase2_quick.js (112 lines)
     - 43 quick tests covering all language features
     - 8 unforgiving rules validation
     - Result: 42/43 passed (97.7% success rate)

   **Phase 3 Files (Module System)**:
   - src/module-loader.js (90 lines)
     - Loads 7 standard modules from src/modules/ directory
     - Singleton pattern for module management
     - require(moduleName) implementation
     - getStatistics() for module function counts
   
   - src/modules/fs.js (490 lines, 25 functions)
     - File reading (5): readFileSync, readFile, readFileAsBuffer, readFileAsJson, readFileAsLines
     - File writing (5): writeFileSync, writeFile, appendFileSync, appendFile, writeFileAsJson
     - File manipulation (8): copyFileSync, copyFile, renameSync, rename, deleteFileSync, deleteFile, truncateSync, truncate
     - File info (7): existsSync, exists, isFileSync, isFile, isDirectorySync, isDirectory, getStatSync
     - All functions return error-wrapped results or throw descriptive errors
   
   - src/modules/os.js (360 lines, 20 functions)
     - System info (6): platform, arch, hostname, type, release, getOSInfo
     - CPU info (5): cpuCount, getCpuInfo, getLoadAverage, getCpuUsage, getCpuCores
     - Memory info (5): getTotalMemory, getFreeMemory, getUsedMemory, getMemoryUsagePercent, getMemoryInfo
     - Network info (4): getNetworkInterfaces, getHostname, getHomeDirectory, getTempDirectory
     - All functions wrapping native Node.js os module
   
   - src/modules/path.js (260 lines, 15 functions)
     - Path analysis (8): dirname, basename, extname, parse, format, relative, normalize, getRoot
     - Path joining (4): join, resolve, cwd, isAbsolute
     - Path manipulation (3): changeExtension, removeExtension, splitPath
     - Cross-platform path handling
   
   - src/modules/crypto.js (~500 lines, 30 functions)
     - Hash functions (6): md5, sha1, sha256, sha512, sha384, hmacSha256
     - Symmetric encryption (8): aesEncrypt, aesDecrypt, aes128Encrypt, aes128Decrypt, desEncrypt, desDecrypt (using CBC mode)
     - Encoding/decoding (8): base64Encode/Decode, hexEncode/Decode, utf8Encode/Decode, urlEncode/Decode
     - Random generation (6): randomInt, randomHex, randomBase64, randomBytes, uuidv4, randomString
     - Key generation (2): generateAes256Key, generateIv
     - All cryptographic operations using Node.js crypto module
   
   - test_phase3_modules.js (149 lines)
     - 22 tests for fs, os, path modules
     - Result: 20/22 passed (90.9% success rate)
     - Module function count verification
     - Module loading validation
   
   - PHASE_2_INTERPRETER_COMPLETION.md (247 lines)
     - Comprehensive Phase 2 completion report
     - Detailed function listings and test results
     - Production readiness assessment (90%)
   
   - PHASE_3_PROGRESS.md (414 lines)
     - Phase 3 Week 1 progress report
     - Detailed module documentation
     - 31.6% overall completion (60/190 functions)

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Postfix Operator Bug**: Parser was incorrectly treating '+' and '-' as postfix operators in the postfix() method, causing expressions like "1 + 2" to parse as "(+1) 2" instead of "1 + 2"
     - Fix: Removed the postfix operator matching code, kept only `return this.call();`
     - Result: Arithmetic operations now work correctly
   
   - **FunctionDeclaration Body Not Wrapped**: Parser was passing raw statement array to FunctionDeclaration instead of BlockStatement
     - Error: "Not a function: object" when calling user-defined functions
     - Fix: Changed `return new FunctionDeclaration(name, params, body)` to wrap statements: `const body = new BlockStatement(statements); return new FunctionDeclaration(name, params, body)`
     - User feedback: Implicitly confirmed fix when tests started passing
   
   - **CallExpression Type Check Order**: Evaluator was checking `typeof callee === 'function'` before `instanceof FreeLangFunction`
     - Error: FreeLangFunction is an object, not a function, so it failed the typeof check
     - Fix: Reordered conditions to check `instanceof FreeLangFunction` first, then `typeof === 'function'`
     - Result: User-defined functions now callable
   
   - **for-in Loop Syntax**: Parser required parentheses after 'for' for all loops, but FreeLang syntax has `for item in arr` without parentheses
     - Error: "Expected ( after for" when parsing for-in loops
     - Fix: Check for for-in pattern first (no parentheses required), restore checkpoint if not for-in, then require parentheses for regular for loop
     - Result: Both `for item in arr {}` and `for (init; test; update) {}` now parse correctly
   
   - **Variable Declaration in for Loop Init**: variableDeclaration() was consuming semicolon, but for loop needs to handle it
     - Error: "Expected variable name" because parser was trying to read identifier after semicolon
     - Fix: Added consumeSemicolon parameter (default true) to variableDeclaration(), call with false in for loop init, manually consume semicolon after
     - Result: for loop with variable declaration now works

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Bootstrap Problem Identification**: Recognized that .fl files written in FreeLang couldn't execute themselves (circular dependency). Solution: Implemented all functions in JavaScript instead, using index.js as bridge.
   - **Function Count Optimization**: Determined 195 was optimal for Phase 1 (avoiding bloat while covering essentials)
   - **Module Architecture**: Designed module loader pattern to mirror Node.js require() system for familiarity
   - **Testing Strategy**: Created quick test suite (43 tests) alongside comprehensive suite to catch issues early
   - **Parser Complexity**: Handled multiple ambiguous grammar cases (for vs for-in, dict vs block, postfix vs binary operators) through lookahead and checkpoint/restore pattern
   - **Scope Management**: Implemented environment chain for proper variable scoping with closure support

6. All user messages:
   - (System context indicated user had completed Phase 1 and started Phase 2)
   - "2 3" - Request to proceed with Steps 2 and 3
   - "다음" (next) - Proceed to next phase
   - "gogs 저장" (save to gogs) - Save progress to repository
   - "프리랭 완성도?" (FreeLang completion status?) - Query about project status
   - "고급은언제해" (when for advanced?) - Question about timeline for advanced features
   - "모두 구현 순서대로" (implement everything in order) - Directive to implement all features sequentially
   - "표준모듈 계획 준비" (prepare standard modules plan) - Request to prepare Phase 3 plan
   - "고" (go/acknowledge) - Confirmation/acknowledgment
   - "시작" (start) - Start Phase 2 implementation
   - [Summary request]
   - "go 3" - Start Phase 3
   - "go" - Continue Phase 3 work

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Complete http module (40 functions) - HTTP client/server functionality
   - Complete date module (35 functions) - Date/time manipulation
   - Complete encoding module (25 functions) - Character/data encoding utilities
   - Integrate remaining 4 modules into module loader
   - Create comprehensive test suite for all Phase 3 modules
   - Create final Phase 3 completion report
   - Achieve 190/190 functions for Phase 3 (currently at 60/190 = 31.6%)
   - Final integration testing of all 385+ functions (195 Phase 1 + ~100 Phase 2 + 190 Phase 3)
   - Commit all Phase 3 work to GOGS

8. Current Work:
   Just completed creation of src/modules/crypto.js with 30 cryptographic functions including:
   - Hash algorithms: MD5, SHA1, SHA256, SHA512, SHA384, HMAC-SHA256
   - Symmetric encryption: AES-256-CBC, AES-128-CBC, DES-CBC (both encrypt and decrypt)
   - Encoding/decoding: Base64, Hex, UTF-8, URL encoding
   - Random generation: randomInt, randomHex, randomBase64, randomBytes, uuidv4, randomString
   - Key generation: generateAes256Key(), generateIv()
   
   Phase 3 module system status:
   - fs module: ✅ Complete (25/25 functions)
   - os module: ✅ Complete (20/20 functions)  
   - path module: ✅ Complete (15/15 functions)
   - crypto module: ✅ Complete (30/30 functions)
   - http module: ⏳ Not started (40 functions pending)
   - date module: ⏳ Not started (35 functions pending)
   - encoding module: ⏳ Not started (25 functions pending)
   
   Current progress: 90/190 Phase 3 functions (47.4%), with module loader fully functional and require() system integrated into evaluator.

9. Optional Next Step:
   User's last explicit request was "go" which means continue with Phase 3 implementation. The immediate next step is to create the http module (40 functions) for HTTP client/server functionality. This includes implementing HTTP request handling, response management, routing capabilities, and middleware support. Following the pattern established with fs, os, path, and crypto modules, this will involve wrapping Node.js http/https modules and creating utility functions for common HTTP operations.

</summary>
